Treaties are interpreted in good faith under Articles 31–33 of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties, which reflect customary international law. Their terms take their ordinary meaning in context and in light of the treaty’s object and purpose, together with any subsequent agreement, subsequent practice, and relevant rules of international law. Preparatory work is a supplementary means, used to confirm that reading or when the text is ambiguous, obscure, or manifestly absurd or unreasonable.
CONFIDENCE: 94
